subject: literature
passage: The letter that arrived in March was addressed in a hand Oksana had not seen in nearly twenty years, and she left it unopened on the hall table for most of a week, walking past it each morning as though it were an ordinary bill. When at last she read it, she learned that her old piano teacher, now in her nineties, had heard Oksana's recording on the radio and wished to tell her how proud she was. ______ Oksana had believed that the teacher, who had dismissed her from lessons with the remark that she lacked discipline, had long since forgotten her, or remembered her only as a failure.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The last sentence uses "had believed," which describes what Oksana thought before she read the letter. The transition must mark that earlier time and show that the letter ended her old belief.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean Oksana held her belief in spite of the letter, but the past perfect "had believed" refers to the time before the letter. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Her belief that the teacher had forgotten her is not a restatement of the letter's message; it is the opposite.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Afterward" would place her belief after reading the letter, but the letter showed that the teacher remembered her with pride, so the belief must come before it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Until then" shows that Oksana held this belief up to the moment she read the letter.
